mappings.note: First part explains the seagull's fear from the text (character, LO-2); the follow-ups about timid birds and human babies ask the learner to speculate for themselves (C-E1.2).
What finally drove the seagull off the ledge is hunger overriding fear - his motivation, LO-2, not a fact to be retrieved.
Why the parents kept calling to him is their motive as characters, LO-2; the quoted line supplies the situation, not the answer.
A 'have you ever' prompt about the learner's own life that never returns to the story. Personal expression, C-E1.2.
Reflects on whether the learner's own success was guaranteed - opinion and reasoning about their own experience, C-E1.2.
A group presentation on aircraft, cars, wingspans or migration. The marked skill is composing and presenting in a set format, C-E1.2; none of the topics is about the text.
Curveting, banking and soaring are the words the text uses for the siblings' flight; retrieval, LO-1.
Authorship of 'His First Flight'. Knowledge about the literary work itself sits in C-E1.4; no LO covers it.
Twenty-four hours is a figure stated in the story; single-fact retrieval, LO-1.
A word-relationship analogy (devour:guzzle::nibble:peck). Vocabulary, C-E1.1, not a grammar or literature outcome.
Who was left on the ledge is narrated outright; retrieval, LO-1.
Asks which option repeats the alliteration of 'shrieking shrilly'. Recognising and applying a sound device is a literary convention, C-E1.4, and no LO names devices.
Retrieval of the same detail from the other side - that he was alone. LO-1.
How the seagull felt about flying is his emotional state, LO-2, rather than a narrated event.
Fill-in of 'flight' from the phrase 'perfecting the art of flight'. Extraction, LO-1.
Which family member watched him is a stated detail; retrieval, LO-1.
Whom he begged for food is narrated; single-fact retrieval.
'Maddened by hunger' is the story's own phrase; fill-in retrieval, LO-1.
The direction of the fall (outward and downward) is described in the text; retrieval.
The reason he dived - wanting the fish, not his mother - is his motive, so LO-2 rather than the plain 'what happened' of LO-1.
Requires inferring why he feigned sleep on one leg: to be noticed. Motive, LO-2; the narration never states it directly.
'Justify the given statement with reference to the baby seagull's fear' asks for an answer built on textual evidence, which is LO-3; LO-2 would cover only describing the fear.
Separates the literal and metaphorical senses of 'plunge'. Metaphor is a literary convention and this frame has no vocabulary LO for figurative language, so C-E1.4.
Hunger as nature's strongest motivator is the story's sub-theme, which LO-1 names. Not C-E1.2: the argument is to come from the story, not from opinion.
'Validate the statement with reference to the baby seagull's fear' is an evidence-based answer, LO-3, rather than free opinion under C-E1.2.
Describes the seagull's emotions in flight - inner state, LO-2.
'How far do you think this was by his choice' invites a judgement the text never settles; opinion with reasoning, C-E1.2.
The mother's trick with the fish is narrated step by step; retrieval, LO-1. The version asking what her plan was is the LO-2 item.
Reports what the parents and siblings did while he hesitated - narrated behaviour, so extraction under LO-1.
The actions he took (standing on one leg, feigning sleep) are described in the text; retrieval, LO-1, while the 'why' version is LO-2.
The experience of the first flight is a sequence of feelings - terror, then exhilaration - so LO-2 rather than a list of events.
Asks what the mother's plan was, i.e. her intention. Motive, LO-2, as against the LO-1 item that just describes the trick.
Traces the change in the seagull's feelings once he accepted he could not fly - emotional state, LO-2.
How the parents taught skimming and diving is narrated; information extraction, LO-1.
What each family member was doing on the plateau is a set of stated details; retrieval.
The family's screaming, praising and offering of scraps is narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
How he felt on finally flying - triumph - is his inner state, LO-2.
The reason for his fear (believing his wings too weak) is his state of mind, LO-2, not a retrievable event.
What he had watched the day before is narrated; retrieval, LO-1.
A humorous composition about the learner's own first attempts at a skill. Style and tone are explicitly marked - C-E1.2, with no return to the text.
